evals.name: add-memory-panel-real-query
evals.prompt: Add a memory panel to the web-red dashboard next to latency so we can see saturation when a service slows down. Our apps run on the argus platform (kubeletstats names are in Mimir).
evals.expected_output: Adds a metric:memory-working-set (or similarly named) panel to the web-red dashboard in profiles/classes/web.yaml AND adds its real PromQL to _METRIC_QUERIES in agent/argus/rendering/perses.py in the same change (otherwise the panel renders the up placeholder). Runs make test, regen-golden (the golden diff shows the new panel with a real query, not up), and make validate so percli judges the rendered dashboard.
assertions: A new metric:* panel appears in the web-red dashboards: block of profiles/classes/web.yaml
A matching PromQL entry is added to _METRIC_QUERIES in agent/argus/rendering/perses.py
The regenerated golden shows the new panel with the real query, not the up placeholder
make test and make validate (percli) pass

evals.name: existing-panel-judgment
evals.prompt: Our podinfo dashboard should show the traces for slow requests right next to the latency panel, can you set that up?
evals.expected_output: Recognizes web-red already co-locates traces:slow-requests beside metric:latency-p99 (the spike-proven correlated-panel mitigation) and verifies it renders for podinfo instead of duplicating the panel. Points at the rendered dashboard or the profile as evidence.
assertions: Does not add a duplicate traces panel to web-red
Identifies that traces:slow-requests already sits beside metric:latency-p99 in the web class profile
Verifies rather than edits (render preview, golden, or live Perses proxy)
